verdict_note: No sign-off. Rule Z1-Z3 is sound and precise on the Rollup document: an implementation written from the contract text equals the instrument atom for atom, and I found no counted non-read, missed read or missed write. But the package can't be built as preregistered. Every I72 atom violates spec/schemas/evidence.schema.json's model and id patterns, so GEVID fails unless the schema changes, which I72-R2 forbids; and Z7 misses earlier tests that fail on a correct build (I66's light-copy check, I14's ID_RE, and I14's 'post' ban unless the walker moves out of evidence.py). P1 is entailed by R3 and R4, so it is not a counted prediction under I66's criterion; the key's disclosure contradicts the prompt about the pre-prereg draft; and the reviewed files are byte-identical to the WIP commit ef6835f, now on top of 2d173e3 (I67's merge).

findings.what: The evidence schema admits only [A-Za-z0-9_]+ as an atom's model and as the model part of its id. I20 keys the adopted model by its file name without .json (morph_rollup.extracted), and Z3/P1 fix that model and id, so every I72 atom is schema-invalid. GEVID validates the committed set; an invalid set is unusable, every law becomes uncovered, and GEVID fails on M0-M3. The only way out is a schema change. Z4/Z6 don't mention one, and I72-R2 forbids it ('no ... other spec/ file'; the schema is not in R2's fixed set). So no correct build can pass both R1 (and R3's CI gates) and R2.
findings.evidence: holon.schema.errors on gen/M2/evidence.json plus the instrument's 421 atoms: 842 errors, e.g. "$.atoms[213].model: 'morph_rollup.extracted' does not match '^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$'", plus the id pattern. Simulated build in a scratch clone (lead 2d173e3; prereg; my transitions_atoms written from Z1-Z4, equal to the instrument atom for atom; holon evidence/derive/lossy/metrics run; merged --no-ff). With the committed schema, E.gevid fails on M0 (10 problems, 8 uncovered), M1 (17, 16), M2 (27, 13) and M3 (273, 135). With the two patterns widened to [A-Za-z0-9_.], GEVID passes on M0-M3 with exactly the pinned mismatches, and then every I72 test passes except I72-R2: "Lists differ: ['spec/schemas/evidence.schema.json'] != []". Also schema-dependent: I14 test_document_validates_against_the_evidence_schema, I24 test_m3_evidence (tests_m3/test_derive_par.py:747), I66 test_the_set_gains_the_view_model_alone (tests_m3/test_view_evidence.py:784). spec/schemas/evidence.schema.json is not in FROZEN.sha256.
findings.fix: State in Z4 that the atom 'model' and 'id' patterns of spec/schemas/evidence.schema.json admit the adopted model key (e.g. model ^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*$, the same group in id), with its description. List the change in Z6 as a build commit. Add the file to R2's fixed set and claim, checked to differ from its parent in those two patterns alone. Mention it in the prompt and the BUILD_PLAN row. Precedent: I67's rule Y4 (c) changed the same schema's facts_version enum.

checked_fine: Instrument reproduces the key on the committed document: 421 atoms, 55 self-pairs, 25 families, the five pinned examples, 92 atoms with an endpoint at challengeState or setPause.

An independent implementation written from Z1-Z4's text equals the instrument atom for atom (421), and holon.diagram.evidence.transitions_atoms placed via build gives P1, R3 and R5 passing on the simulated build.

Z1 on the real document. Every ['storage', X] names a declared family; only __gap is declared twice, and it is never accessed. Effects families equal write-record families in all 33 actions. Every store path in post or loop records has a matching write record, so no write is visible only as threading. Store path segments are map/member only. Post keys and loop ['storage', f] names are all declared families.

Reads with non-storage bases are genuine: revertBatch reads committedBatches[_batchIndex+1] through a store base in next/break; challengeState reads batchDataStore[i].finalizeTimestamp through a carried base (+= proofWindow); revertBatch reads revertReqIndex through carried in the write cond. The threading exclusion hides no read: '?' conditions, store keys and values, and other families' terms in threading positions are all counted. For example, revertBatch writes inChallenge but never reads it, and the instrument gives no read.

Every section is walked (guards with reaches, principal, checks, events, calls, mstores, panics, returns, cost, loop head/cond/bound/count/break/regions); event, return and cost reads are pre-state reads of the action.

Z2/Z3 vs I14: same symbolic-overlaps-all rule. Member separation and the threading exclusion are refinements: I14's walker likewise doesn't count f := set_at(f, ...) or '?' branches as reads of f, but does count a 'with' record update as a whole read. No atom beyond I14's semantics; via/id scheme as I14's _atom.

Z4's exclusions hold in holon: both in-memory builds (holon/rules/__init__.py:551, holon/codecrun.py:171) pass diagrams and adopted=False; GEVID and `holon evidence` go through build_milestone; gate G1 doesn't regenerate the set.
